title: Brazil is a warning for the world
gist: Writer Eliane Brum argues Brazil's presidential runoff between Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro is existential for the Amazon, as fires have doubled since round one, Bolsonarism dominates Congress and Amazon governorships, and a Bolsonaro win would accelerate deforestation and align South America with Trump.

insights.claim: Brazil harbours 60 per cent of the largest tropical rainforest, a vital carbon sink, so its election outcome materially affects global climate and biodiversity efforts.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Brazil's election is a climate-policy event with global spillovers.
insights.locator: To understand what is at stake in the Brazilian elections

insights.claim: The Lula government cut Amazon deforestation by nearly 50 per cent, and a win by Flavio Bolsonaro would all but guarantee increased deforestation with a free pass for exploitation.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Election result is a binary driver for Amazon deforestation trajectories and related carbon and commodity policy.

insights.claim: Forest fires in the Amazon have doubled since the 4 October first round, compared with 1,457 fire hotspots on the 2019 'Fire Day' organised on WhatsApp to support Jair Bolsonaro.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Fire counts are a real-time gauge of expected enforcement collapse tied to electoral outcomes.

insights.claim: Informants warn that armed intruders and gold miners are gathering at Indigenous territory borders, ready to invade if the far right wins.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Illegal mining and land grabs are priced to surge on a Bolsonaro win.

insights.claim: In round one Flavio Bolsonaro received 2.2m more votes than Lula, and the newly elected Congress will be dominated by Bolsonarism and be more predatory than the previous one.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Even a Lula win would face a hostile legislature, limiting reform capacity.

insights.claim: Seven of the Amazon's nine governors have ties to Bolsonarism, including Para's Daniel Santos, fined roughly $275,000 for deforestation and elected pledging to cancel environmental fines.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Subnational control by deforestation-friendly politicians undermines federal enforcement.
insights.locator: seven of the Amazon’s nine governors

insights.claim: Brazil's supreme court is weakened by the Banco Master scandal, Brazil's largest-ever financial fraud case, reducing its ability to check Congress's unconstitutional moves.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Institutional weakness raises governance risk for Brazil regardless of the election result.
insights.locator: Brazil’s supreme court has been mired

insights.claim: A Flavio Bolsonaro victory would put nearly all of South America under Donald Trump's tutelage.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Regional alignment shift would matter for trade, geopolitics, and climate diplomacy.
insights.locator: It would also mean nearly all of South America

insights.claim: Brum argues Bolsonarism is a fascist project, not a left-right contest, and that the far right does not share power, a lesson for right-wing parties elsewhere that align strategically with extremists.
insights.speaker: Eliane Brum
insights.so_what: Frames coalition-with-extremists risk for centre-right parties.
insights.quote: Bolsonarism is a fascist project that aims to perpetuate itself in power
insights.locator: No, these elections are not normal.
